sketch: Instead of a coined discrete-time walk, use a continuous-time quantum walk (CTQW) with adjacency Hamiltonian H=A on a small graph, compiled as exp(-i t A) via exact diagonalisation into a unitary gate. Smallest instance: the 4-cycle C4, which is the 2-cube Q2=K2 box K2, so A=X⊗I+I⊗X (commuting terms). Then U(t)=exp(-i t X)⊗exp(-i t X), and at t=pi/2 gives (-iX)⊗(-iX)=-(X⊗X), mapping node |00> to |11>, which is the antipodal node, with fidelity 1 (perfect state transfer). Encoding: node label n in {0,1,2,3} as 2 qubits with Gray-code order 0->00, 1->01, 2->11, 3->10 so that cycle neighbours differ by one bit and antipodes are bitwise complements. Steps: (1) prepare |00>; (2) apply Rx(pi) on each qubit, i.e. exp(-i(pi/2)X) on each, which is the CTQW unitary at t=pi/2; (3) read out the node distribution and check that amplitude is concentrated on |11> (the antipode). Robustness probes, as the abstract suggests: perturb the initial state, add a weight-interpolation parameter w on a chord or edge, H(w)=A+wB, and evaluate the fidelity |<antipode|exp(-i t H(w))|start>|^2 versus w. Decoherence is outside the circuit, since a unitary-only interface cannot represent it. Generalisation to n nodes is by weighted or modified families, where PST would require the eigenvalue and parity conditions on H; those families are not specified in the abstract. Why this achieves the claim: it is the continuous-time analogue showing antipodal PST on the modified/C4 structure, with an exact unitary and a checkable output. It is a narrower task than the paper: it covers only C4, only the CTQW, and does not reproduce the C6/C8 modifications, the three coin choices, or the three graph families.
